topic: The Magic of Topology: Solving the Stolen Necklace Problem via Borsuk-Ulam
target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with an interest in geometry and logic

sections.title: The Hook: The Fair Thief Dilemma
lecture_lines: Two thieves steal a necklace with different bead types.
They want to share every type exactly in half.
What is the minimum number of cuts needed?
animations: A horizontal line appears with 10 red circles (#FF0000) and 8 blue circles (#0000FF) distributed randomly along it.
Two stick figures, labeled 'Thief A' and 'Thief B', appear on the left and right sides of the necklace respectively.
A question mark appears above the thieves with the text 'Fair split with minimal cuts?' (#FFFFFF) centered above the necklace.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Antipodal Points and Mapping
lecture_lines: Antipodal points are directly opposite on a circle or sphere.
Every point x has an opposite partner -x.
We can map these points to values like temperature.
animations: A white circle (#FFFFFF) appears. A point 'x' is marked on the perimeter with a small dot.
A dashed line segment passes through the center of the circle to the exact opposite side, marking the point '-x'.
A color gradient representing a function f(x) (e.g., temperature) flows around the circle's circumference.

sections.title: The Core: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
lecture_lines: The Borsuk-Ulam theorem relates spheres to continuous functions.
It states pairs of antipodal points map to same values.
Imagine measuring temperature and pressure anywhere on Earth.
Two opposite spots always share the exact same conditions.
This holds true for any continuous mapping on spheres.
animations: A 2D projection of a sphere representing Earth appears, with two opposite points highlighted with glowing pulses.
Temperature labels 'T1' and 'T2' appear at the antipodal points, then change to show 'T1 = T2' (#00FF00).
Pressure labels 'P1' and 'P2' appear at the same points, then change to show 'P1 = P2' (#00FFFF).
The text 'Borsuk-Ulam Theorem' fades in at the top of the screen in a bold font (#FFFFFF).
A mapping arrow points from the sphere to a 2D plane where the point (T, P) is plotted.

sections.title: Connecting the Dots: Beads to Functions
lecture_lines: We can model the necklace as a continuous loop.
A single cut point is like a position on a circle.
Let f(x) be the amount of beads Thief A gets.
As we move the cut, this share changes continuously.
Multiple bead types require higher-dimensional spheres and mappings.
animations: The linear necklace from the start bends and joins its ends to form a circle (#FFFFFF).
A pair of scissors icons appear on the circle, representing potential cut locations.
A dynamic bar chart appears next to the circle, showing the 'Share of Red' and 'Share of Blue' for Thief A.
The scissors move along the circle, and the bars on the chart rise and fall smoothly in response.
The text 'Positions map to a sphere' appears, linking the cut locations to the Borsuk-Ulam setup (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Mathematical Solution: The k-cut Proof
lecture_lines: For k bead types, we use a k-dimensional sphere.
A point on this sphere defines k cut locations.
Borsuk-Ulam guarantees antipodal points with identical bead shares.
If Thief A gets half, Thief B must also.
Thus, only k cuts ensure a perfectly fair split.
animations: A necklace with 2 types of beads is shown with 2 cut marks at specific positions.
A mathematical vector (diff_red, diff_blue) is displayed, representing the difference between the two thieves' shares.
The cut marks adjust until the vector (diff_red, diff_blue) becomes (0, 0) (#00FF00).
The necklace is cut at these points, and the beads are sorted into two identical piles.
A balance scale appears with the two piles of beads, showing they are perfectly equal in weight and composition.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Abstraction
lecture_lines: Topology turns a discrete puzzle into a geometric solution.
Simple properties of spheres solve complex division problems.
This is the hidden power of mathematical abstraction.
animations: The necklace circle morphs into a smooth sphere, which then morphs into the text 'Topology' (#00FFFF).
The words 'Discrete Problem' and 'Continuous Solution' appear on opposite sides of a double-headed arrow.
The two thieves (stick figures) reappear, smiling and holding their equal shares of the necklace.
